answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce token as a bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits prove fraud. Because one attacker cannot cheaply multiply the same locked capital, creating a thousand Sybils means funding a thousand bonds and keeping them tied up; if caught, the stake is lost. A cipher can protect private audit evidence, while a ridge of repeated failures marks a relic identity that earns no trust.
